purpose: Reversible projection of arbitrary source documents into a JSON-object envelope containing reusable functional opcodes and stable source-linked records.

supported_source_formats.json: Valid JSON parsed into records with JSON Pointers; original UTF-8 bytes preserved in the envelope.
supported_source_formats.utf8_text: Unicode text segmented into line views; original bytes remain authoritative.
supported_source_formats.opaque_binary: Arbitrary bytes preserved in base64 with one uninterpreted capture record. Content extraction requires a separately implemented format-specific parser.

distinction.procedure_opcode: IS.* identifiers uniquely identify normative AGENTS.md clauses. They do not represent reusable functions.
distinction.operation_opcode: OP.01.* identifies a reusable action from the registry. Multiple records and documents may use the same opcode.
distinction.record_id: Original source ID if supplied; otherwise a stable ordinal identity within that conversion. Not an opcode.
distinction.domain_function: A registered implementation of an opcode for a concrete domain; not generated or inferred by the generic adapter.

source_envelope.required_property: Exact original file bytes reconstructible from canonical base64, checked against SHA-256.
source_envelope.authoritative: Stored source.bytes_base64 overrides any projections in case of disagreement; validation should reject the disagreement.

record_shape.capture_rule: First step is CAPTURE with original source pointer.
record_shape.emit_rule: Last step is EMIT; these are declarations, not execution receipts.
record_shape.default: CAPTURE -> EMIT with mapping_status=capture_only; do not guess semantic operations from arbitrary prose.
record_shape.explicit_mapping: An externally provided mapping profile supplies intermediate operation opcodes; all opcodes must belong to the documented registry.

procedure.action: Load original bytes and select the appropriate source extractor; default to opaque preservation for unsupported formats.
Compute canonical byte length and SHA-256, and retain exact original bytes in base64 before any transformation.
Extract source-linked records and assign record identities separately from functional opcodes.
Assign CAPTURE and EMIT; add only explicitly mapped, registry-valid intermediate operator opcodes.
Output one valid JSON object holding source, conversion metadata, and operation-coded records. Never replace or mutate the original document.
Verify byte-for-byte restoration, source digest, record coverage, pointers, original values, text fields, opcode validity, and step ordering.
Refuse unrecognized opcodes, duplicated identities, invalid mappings, and loss of source provenance; report errors instead of silently dropping source material.
Keep opcode classification separate from execution and semantic assessment; never claim that output instructions have been performed.

limitations: Content inside binary PDFs, images, DOCX or other binary files is preserved but not extracted without dedicated parsers.
Structural conversion does not imply semantic understanding or equivalence of task interpretations.
Core function opcodes are finite and reusable; concrete task performance additionally requires domain-specific functions and arguments.
These JSON-object documents do not replace the required scratchpad-wrapped array for final RS records.
